title.narrative: Mozambique Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Program

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to strengthen the Government of Mozambique's program to finance and prepare for disaster response and to increase the climate resilience of vulnerable education infrastructure in risk-prone areas.

The development objective of Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Program Project is to strengthen the government of Mozambique's (GoM) program to finance and prepare for disaster response and to increase the climate resilience of vulnerable education infrastructure in risk prone areas. The program will support a subset of results identified under strategic objectives two, three, and four of the government program. The results and activities to be supported under the Program for Results (PforR) have been prioritized with the GoM based on the most urgent challenges for which they requested support, considering readiness for implementation, building on previous World Bank support to DRM and findings from recent analytical work, and aiming to complement other Bank/donor-financed projects in Mozambique. This results area will focus on improving financial preparedness for disasters, i.e. increasing the availability, predictability, and efficiency of ex-ante resources for disaster preparedness and response. This will be achieved through: (i) the operationalization of the Disaster Management Fund (DMF); (ii) the recurrent capitalization of the DMF and implementation of audit recommendations; and (iii) developing the capacity of GoM to enable the placement of sovereign catastrophe insurance coverage for cyclones and/or drought with capital or insurance markets.

condition.narrative: Within six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall adopt the POM, as approved by the Association and thereafter,implement the Program and Project in accordance with the POM.

title.narrative: Ex-ante resources immediately available annually for disaster preparedness and response

comment.narrative: By adopting the DMF Decree, the GoM committed to transferring 0.1% of the annual state budget to the Disaster Management Fund (DMF) each year. At Program closure, all results for years 1 to 5 have been achieved, and verified by the Administrative Tribunal and payment made for years 1 to 4. Payment for year 5 will not be made as for recovery of advance of US$11.66 million made by the Bank in 2019. In total, the Government has allocated a total amount of MZM 2,857 million (corresponding to US$45.15 million) to the Disaster Management Fund. The Bank has disbursed the total amount of US$31 million against the achievement of Prior results and results for years 1-4, while a cumulative amount of US$78.15 million was already disbursed to the DMF by Government and the Bank.

title.narrative: New or strengthened local DRM committees with at least 50% of female committee members created or trained

comment.narrative: 1,500 Local committees have been strengthened across the country covering 3 million people. 50% of the members of these committees are women.

title.narrative: Number of classrooms in risk-prone areas retrofitted or reconstructed in accordance with climate-resilient technical norms under the Program
Risk transfer products for cyclone and/or drought risk have undergone an external technical review

comment.narrative: The Government hired a consortium of insurance firms on November 4, 2022, and signed the first insurance policy in December 2022, in the amount of US$4 million to provide coverage against cyclone winds and excessive rainfall in the cyclonic season of 2022/2023. The two risk transfer products designed by the broker were externally reviewed by the firm that designed the catastrophe model. The risk transfer products for 2023/2024 and 2024/2025 were signed in December 2023 and April 2024, respectively and were subject to external verification by the independent firm that verified the policy of 2022/2023.

title.narrative: National School Database upgraded and updated with data from building assessment

comment.narrative: The National School database is operational and was still in the process of being updated at the time of Program closure

title.narrative: Annual independent audits on use of funds under DMF completed and recommendations implemented

comment.narrative: Audit reports were on track by closure, with the 2023 and 2024 reports under preparation

title.narrative: Stand-by contracts for disaster response signed with at least two firms annually

comment.narrative: The Government hired a consortium of insurance firms on November 4, 2022, and signed the first insurance policy in December 2022, in the amount of US$4 million to provide coverage against cyclone winds and excessive rainfall in the cyclonic season of 2022/2023. The Government has received a payout of US$904.304 for the impacts of cyclone Freddy, of which US$642.882 for the impacts of cyclone winds and US$261.422 for excessive rains. The Government placed contracts for similar insurance policies for the rainy season of 2023/2024 (by mid-December 2023) and 2024/2025 (in April 2024).

title.narrative: Sovereign catastrophe insurance coverage for at least one peril (cyclone and/or drought) with capital or insurance market in place, in accordance with national Disaster Risk Finance Strategy

comment.narrative: The Government hired a consortium of insurance firms on November 4, 2022, and signed the first insurance policy in December 2022, in the amount of US$4 million to provide coverage against cyclone winds and excessive rainfall in the cyclonic season of 2022/2023. The Government has received a payout of US$904.304 for the impacts of cyclone Freddy, of which US$642.882 for the impacts of cyclone winds and US$261.422 for excessive rains. title.narrative: MOUs between INAM, DNGRH, and INGD are established or revised

comment.narrative: The MOU was elevated to a Decree of the Council of Ministers. The Decree n. 27/2022, of June 6, approving the establishment of the platform and the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for early warning information flow between INAM, DNGRH, and INGD was approved by Cabinet and published in the national gazette on June 6, 2022

title.narrative: Ministerial diploma adopting technical norms for climate-resilient education infrastructure in place

comment.narrative: The Ministerial Diploma adopting technical norms for climate-resilient education infrastructure was signed by the Ministers of MOPHRH and MINEDH and published in the national gazette (Ministerial Diploma No. 122/2021, of October 26. The Diploma is being widely used by the construction industry, including with adaptations for the resilient construction and rehabilitation of health units and housing.

title.narrative: Maintenance arrangements for the rehabilitated school infrastructure developed and implemented

comment.narrative: The Ministerial Diploma approved by Government in October 2021 includes provisions for the maintenance of education infrastructure.

title.narrative: National Disaster Risk Finance Strategy developed and adopted

comment.narrative: The Strategy was changed to a Plan in line with the provisions of the new Law of the Public Financial Administration System- e-Sistafe (Law n.15/2020, of December 23). The DRFI Plan was approved by the Cabinet on June 28, 2022.

title.narrative: Number of people in risk-prone areas reached by flood and cyclone early warning systems under the Program

comment.narrative: The system was set in October 2023 and tested by the end of December 2023, and messages were delivered through this system to people at risk of cyclones, floods and heavy rains across the country, including the 1,9 million targeted by the Program of which 700,000 people in Gaza and Inhambane provinces and 1,200,000 people in Zambezia province between December 2023 and April 2024.

title.narrative: Number of children provided with access to climate-resilient education infrastructure under the Program

comment.narrative: 1,018 classrooms retrofitted or reconstructed by Program closure, providing climate-resilient education infrastructure to 122,160 students.

title.narrative: Number of people in risk-prone areas covered by functioning local DRM committees under the Program

comment.narrative: 1,500 Local DRM Committees covering 3 million people have been strengthened across the country, with the strengthening of the last 124 committees in the provinces of Nampula and Niassa completed in June 2024.

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of Program benefits that are actually addressed (MINEDH)

comment.narrative: 90.2% of complaints received have been handled and the others are being addressed

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of Program benefits that are actually addressed (INGC)

comment.narrative: From January-June 2024, INGD has received a total of 1,016 total complaints, of which 985 had been resolved and closed by Program closure

title.narrative: Number of functional local DRM committees in risk-prone areas established or strengthened

comment.narrative: 1,500 Local Committees have been strengthened across the country and serving 3 million people.
